english.note: Use 搵 as the all-purpose spoken verb for looking for something, including searching around a place.
This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for trying to find or look for something.
This is the all-purpose choice for trying to find something.
Use this when searching among other things to find or get hold of something.
Use 搵 when looking means searching for or trying to find something.

examples.english: I had to search around for an hour before I found the book.
examples.traditional: 我周圍搵咗成個鐘先搵到本書。
examples.jyutping: ngo5 zau1 wai4 wan2 zo2 seng4 go3 zung1 sin1 wan2 dou2 bun2 syu1

examples.english: I want to seek out a job near home.
examples.jyutping: ngo5 soeng2 wan2 fan6 gan6 uk1 kei2 ge3 gung1

examples.english: I still have to hunt for my keys.
examples.jyutping: ngo5 zung6 jiu3 wan2 ngo5 di1 so2 ci4

examples.english: I fish through my bag for my Octopus card.
examples.traditional: 我喺個袋入面搵張八達通。
examples.jyutping: ngo5 hai2 go3 doi6 jap6 min6 wan2 zoeng1 baat3 daat6 tung1

examples.english: I look everywhere but still can't find the book.
examples.traditional: 我周圍搵都搵唔到本書。
examples.jyutping: ngo5 zau1 wai4 wan2 dou1 wan2 m4 dou2 bun2 syu1
